finding: Tax information may have shaped the powertrain choice
evidence_paraphrase: Owner says they bought a 2025 Reborn diesel after browsing/asking about a higher annual tax on a Zenix hybrid. They express regret after seeing a lower figure.
limitation: The post establishes the owner's reported information process, not the correct tax or a causal counterfactual. Parent/root are missing.
test_implication: Test verified city/year/variant-specific tax information alongside financing and household fit.

finding: Household capacity competes with design, features and available cash
evidence_paraphrase: Poster lists Fronx, XL7 and Veloz Hybrid, distinguishes two versus three rows, states Batam prices and says cash must first be accumulated.
limitation: No completed transaction, current vehicle, Auto2000 history or verified quote.
test_implication: Compare shortlist usefulness on a real household task; financing capacity may remain binding.

evidence_type: self-reported purchase with unrelated business promotion appended
finding: Upgrade economics can be expressed as a net cash gap
evidence_paraphrase: Poster says an Avanza sold for Rp190m and a Veloz Hybrid was purchased at Rp354m, with fuel savings and comfort motivating the change.
limitation: Rp164m is arithmetic on reported prices before loan settlement, fees and other adjustments. Retailer and actual settlement route are unknown. Fuel savings are unverified.
test_implication: Use a net-upgrade-cost prototype with an explicit loan payoff, fees, quote status and next step.

finding: Fuel savings do not automatically mean perceived total ownership value
evidence_paraphrase: Yaris Cross Hybrid owner praises fuel economy but complains about tax, insurance, service cost and falling resale value.
limitation: No invoice, job, dates of charges or realized resale transaction; immediate parent missing.
test_implication: Distinguish scheduled covered service, paid jobs, tax and insurance before comparing total costs.

finding: Owners may choose different workshop channels for different brands
evidence_paraphrase: Poster says Toyota and Chinese-brand cars go to official workshops, whereas Honda/Mazda go to community workshops.
limitation: No job-level switching episode, price or Auto2000 identification.
test_implication: Investigate perceived capability, trust and parts access; do not assume owners uniformly avoid official workshops.

finding: Bill and repair-trust complaints merit verification
evidence_paraphrase: Poster recounts a friend's Calya clutch and AC bill and a subsequent clutch problem.
limitation: Third-party allegation; workshop identity, invoice, work scope and diagnosis are not established. No Auto2000 attribution.
test_implication: Use as an interview prompt about scope approval and parts traceability, not verified misconduct.

finding: Family transitions can support continued used-Toyota ownership
evidence_paraphrase: Poster describes Camry to Innova to Fortuner and back to Innova, always used, prioritizing family comfort and repair access.
limitation: No Auto2000 purchase history or xEV purchase; continuity with Toyota is not a qualified new-car lead.
test_implication: Include used-versus-new and retain-current-car alternatives in the replacement journey.

finding: An owner may manage resale risk using operating savings
evidence_paraphrase: Poster describes six months of savings and setting money aside against future resale loss.
limitation: Vehicle, baseline, amounts and earlier thread sections are missing. No verified net total-cost saving.
test_implication: Recover the earlier thread and seek contrasting ownership strategies before proposing a guarantee.

finding: Inspection is already discussed as a purchasable service
evidence_paraphrase: Community account suggests inspecting a used Toyota hybrid at an official workshop, recalling an Auto2000 inspection fee.
limitation: The remembered price is uncertain and not a branch quote, certificate acceptance or completed inspection.
test_implication: Check the existing service and appraiser acceptance before creating another certificate.

finding: Service records and battery-condition claims already appear in seller positioning
evidence_paraphrase: Seller advertises an Altis Hybrid with Auto2000 records and a healthy certified battery.
limitation: Not proof of certificate validity, appraisal acceptance, realized premium or completed sale.
test_implication: Test whether the named appraiser accepts the existing evidence and changes an offer.

finding: A published future-value/upgrade promise is a novelty-check lead
evidence_paraphrase: Post advertises a SmartDrive 70% resale-value proposition and a third-year upgrade route with stated conditions.
limitation: Uploaded text is not the full contract, current eligibility confirmation, funding commitment or evidence of customer use.
test_implication: Verify programme terms and responsible counterparties before proposing a new value guarantee.

finding: Repeated SmartDrive messaging is not independent confirmation
evidence_paraphrase: A second post from the same account advertises the SmartDrive upgrade proposition.
limitation: Same publisher and claim family as C11; no independent uptake evidence.
test_implication: Group both posts into one programme-claim family.

finding: Post-warranty economy channels are already part of discussion
evidence_paraphrase: Community post links warranty expiry, independent workshops, CARfix and an economy workshop network.
limitation: It does not measure the share leaving dealers, validate commercial relationships or prove price advantage.
test_implication: Verify OtoXpert/T-OPT capability, participating outlets and contribution ownership.

finding: An upgrade comparison can combine cash difference and use value
evidence_paraphrase: Poster asks whether adding Rp100m to move from an older Avanza to an XL7 is worth the comfort, maintenance and efficiency change.
limitation: Other-brand and non-confirmed purchase; no xEV or Auto2000-history proof.
test_implication: Use as an adjacent design case for understandable upgrade economics.

finding: Specific incidents cannot be recovered from a generic ownership story
evidence_paraphrase: Long narrative describes a friend's EV trip, charging failure, a mechanic discussion and claimed subsequent research.
limitation: No named model, branch, receipts or source records. Claimed interviews inside the post are not this project's interviews.
test_implication: Treat as a narrative to challenge, not verified EV failure or causal education evidence.

finding: First-person grammar can misclassify fiction as a purchase
evidence_paraphrase: The post initially describes a Ford Everest purchase and ends by saying it is an April Fools creative-writing example.
limitation: Exclude from actual buyer accounts regardless of persuasive detail or engagement.
test_implication: Add satire/fiction checks before purchase-outcome classification.

evidence_type: sales listing with inconsistent vehicle framing
finding: Powertrain cannot safely be inferred from one keyword
evidence_paraphrase: The descriptive review contrasts Zenix with a hybrid sibling while the listing specifies a Zenix Q Hybrid.
limitation: Commercial and internally ambiguous; no independent product assessment or confident powertrain label.
test_implication: Use ambiguous powertrain until exact vehicle evidence resolves the inconsistency.

evidence_type: self-reported brand use plus broad complaint
finding: Service trust concerns may coexist with longstanding Toyota use
evidence_paraphrase: Poster identifies longstanding Toyota use and complains about fuel loss at official workshops. A separate reply in the export echoes the experience.
limitation: No named workshop, completed-job details or verified explanation. The second account is conversational corroboration, not causal verification.
test_implication: Ask about handover records, job communication and explanations, retaining positive accounts as contrasts.

finding: Official workshop retention is a necessary counterexample
evidence_paraphrase: Poster describes Freed/Fortuner ownership and consistently using official workshops while discussing replacement batteries.
limitation: Not a measured retention rate or evidence about Auto2000 specifically.
test_implication: Recruit loyal official-workshop users alongside switchers.

finding: Heavy use may sustain official-service demand
evidence_paraphrase: Poster describes a heavily used Veloz and monthly official Toyota workshop care.
limitation: Job mix, commercial use, paid-versus-covered status and dates are not established.
test_implication: Test job and usage intensity rather than assuming a uniform maintenance cadence.

evidence_type: community advice plus self-reported other-brand service
finding: Capability can depend on vehicle age and technician familiarity
evidence_paraphrase: Poster mentions servicing an older Taft at an official Daihatsu workshop and suggests older technicians may understand older cars better.
limitation: Other-brand experience and general advice; not a measured Toyota capacity problem.
test_implication: Validate branch/job/technician capability for the chosen older-Toyota job.

finding: A credible specialist may substitute for an official workshop
evidence_paraphrase: Account recommends considering nearby official, specialist or trusted general workshops before buying a used car.
limitation: Advice does not establish where the author paid for their last job.
test_implication: Benchmark local trusted specialists, not just the cheapest generic garage.

finding: Retailer responsibility and payment provenance can matter in handoff failures
evidence_paraphrase: Poster recounts alleged problems with another brand's dealer, trade-in, payments and complaint handling.
limitation: Unverified third-party allegation; not evidence against Auto2000 or a verified regulatory finding.
test_implication: Use only as an adjacent scenario for official quote/payment channels and accountable ownership.

finding: Stated interest need not indicate a qualified near-term buyer
evidence_paraphrase: Poster expresses interest in EV running-cost savings and concern about resale, then says available money is only Rp2m.
limitation: No quote, credit eligibility or completed purchase; humor complicates seriousness.
test_implication: Separate curiosity, serious shopping and financially qualified next steps.

finding: Jokes are discourse evidence, not demand estimates
evidence_paraphrase: Post lists technical barriers as crossed out and says lack of money is the reason for not buying.
limitation: Not a verified abandoned transaction or willingness-to-pay observation.
test_implication: Use only to motivate an affordability probe, not estimate lost sales.

finding: A brand rejection is not an aftersales experience
evidence_paraphrase: Poster ranks hybrid alternatives and says to skip Chery.
limitation: No Chery ownership, service interaction, job or reason supplied.
test_implication: Do not count this as a Chery aftersales complaint.

finding: An apparent waiting-time complaint is actually brand copy
evidence_paraphrase: Auto2000-branded post imagines a cancelled date after waiting at a workshop and promotes Digiroom booking.
limitation: Not an independent customer's failed booking or appointment outcome.
test_implication: Classify source role before sentiment; keep brand promises separate from fulfillment evidence.
